skill.description: Generate AI video prompts and run inference.sh video models through the belt CLI for text-to-video, image-to-video, lipsync, editing, upscaling, and sound workflows.
skill.summary: Create AI videos and video-processing jobs with inference.sh models through the belt CLI.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: The static backtick detections are mixed: most model IDs, markdown fences, and documentation URLs are false positives, but the skill intentionally runs belt CLI commands. The main residual risk is controlled external CLI use that can submit prompts and media references to inference.sh services.

remediation.issue: The skill can run remote belt CLI commands for video generation.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit user confirmation guidance before running belt commands, especially when prompts, private media URLs, audio, or video files are involved.

remediation.issue: The README suggests installing additional skills with npx commands.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review each related skill and package source before installation, and avoid chaining installs automatically.

remediation.issue: Example media URLs could hide the fact that user assets may be processed by a remote service.
remediation.suggestion: State that media URLs and prompts are sent to external inference.sh applications when belt app run is executed.

content.user_title: Create AI Videos with Inference.sh Models
content.value_statement: AI video teams need clear model choices and repeatable commands. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code run inference.sh video workflows through belt.
actual_capabilities: Lists supported text-to-video models, including Veo, Seedance, HappyHorse, Wan, Grok, and P-Video.
Provides belt CLI examples for text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video, and video editing jobs.
Shows workflows for avatar animation, lipsync, video upscaling, sound effects, and media merging.
Maps model IDs to common production needs such as speed, quality, audio support, and resolution.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps, streaming results, and content pipeline examples.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account before jobs can run.
Generated media quality, cost, duration, and availability depend on the selected remote model.
Media URLs and prompts may be sent to external inference.sh services when belt commands run.
The skill provides command guidance; it does not include local video rendering or model weights.

use_cases.title: Draft Social Video Concepts
use_cases.description: Create short video prompts and choose fast models for social clips, storyboards, and campaign variants.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Images
use_cases.description: Turn product images or references into motion tests with image-to-video and reference-to-video models.

use_cases.title: Build Avatar Workflows
use_cases.description: Prepare talking head, lipsync, sound effect, and upscaling jobs for AI avatar production pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Basic Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a model for a 5 second product teaser. I need fast results and optional audio. Give the belt command and explain each input.

prompt_templates.title: Create Image Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an image URL and want subtle camera movement. Recommend an image-to-video model, write the belt command, and include a concise motion prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Avatar Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow for a talking head video from a portrait and an audio file. Compare OmniHuman and Fabric, then provide the safest command structure.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a three-step AI video pipeline for a launch campaign. Include generation, sound effects, upscaling, and merging. Mention data sent to external services.

output_examples.input: User asks for a fast AI video from a product prompt.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a fast Veo or Seedance model, writes a belt command, and explains prompt, duration, and audio options.

output_examples.input: User provides a portrait URL and narration URL.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a lipsync or avatar model, warns that media URLs are sent externally, and prepares the required command inputs.

output_examples.input: User wants to improve a silent generated clip.
output_examples.output: The assistant suggests a foley model, an upscaler, and a media merge step to produce a finished video asset.

best_practices: Review prompts and media URLs before running belt commands against remote services.
Start with fast or economical models for drafts, then use higher quality models for final clips.
Keep generated commands focused on one model job so errors and costs are easier to track.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential media, private voices, or unreleased product footage without approval.
Do not run broad command changes when a smaller belt job can test the workflow.
Do not assume one model supports every input type, duration, resolution, or audio option.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI video jobs for text prompts, images, references, avatars, lipsync, editing, upscaling, and sound effects.

faq.question: Does it run models locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the belt CLI to call remote inference.sh applications.

faq.question: Which AI assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that the inference.sh belt CLI must be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can it animate existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes image-to-video and reference-to-video examples for several supported models.

faq.question: What should users check before running commands?
faq.answer: Users should check cost, model availability, permissions for media, and whether external service upload is acceptable.
